description: A request to buy service credits, raised by a Rest deployment. DRAFT means requested and unpaid; SUBMITTED means money has been received and the credits are claimable by the app. The draft-to-submitted step is the whole point: only a person, or a payment gateway's own script, can submit, so nothing a tenant application says can make credits real on its own.

fields.label: Purchase Reference
fields.description: The reference this proposal is identified by, and what a payment is matched against. Unique PER DEPLOYMENT -- a composite index, because two churches may legitimately use the same number -- and ALWAYS present: the deployment sends its own if the customer has one, and the app mints a short readable one otherwise. Field-level uniqueness is deliberately NOT set: this Frappe honours `unique: 1` with a GLOBAL index, which would refuse the second church's identical number.

fields.label: Request Key
fields.description: The deployment's own identifier for this purchase. It is the idempotency key: a retried request must resolve to THIS proposal rather than raise a second one, because a duplicate is a request for money nobody asked for. Internal -- never shown to anyone.

fields.label: Payment URL
fields.description: Set by the deployment when a payment link has been created, so the customer can pay. Its presence on an unsettled proposal IS the 'awaiting payment' state -- derived rather than stored, because every stored status is a branch that has to be handled everywhere, and a derived one is handled where it is read.

fields.label: Sales Invoice
fields.description: The invoice raised for this proposal, so it can be paid. Raised when the proposal is created -- an unpaid proposal with no invoice is a request for money the customer cannot act on. Read-only: it is set once by the server, and a second invoice for one proposal would be a second request for the same money.

fields.label: Rest Instance
fields.description: The Rest deployment that asked. A Link, so the identifier resolves to a record carrying the deployment's name and activity.

fields.label: Buyer Email
fields.description: Where the receipt goes when this proposal settles. Optional: a purchase raised by the app may name no buyer, and the receipt step skips rather than fails in that case. Never used to identify the purchase -- identity is the organization, the funding group and the reference.

fields.label: Channel
fields.description: SMS and email credit are separate balances and are never interchangeable.

fields.label: Units
fields.description: Service units requested: SMS segments or email messages. An integer, never a float.

fields.label: Amount (minor units)
fields.description: What the deployment quoted, in the currency's MINOR units. A settler may correct it: a payment that arrives for a different amount is a fact about money that moved, and refusing it would strand a real payment. The settled amount wins and the difference is recorded.

fields.label: Unit Price (micros)
fields.description: The price this purchase was quoted at, in millionths of a major unit. Pricing is pinned when the app raises the request and never re-priced.

fields.label: Settlement
fields.description: Filled in when the money has been received. This is the part the Rest app can never do for itself.

fields.label: Payment Document Type
fields.description: What kind of document records the payment: "Payment Entry" for the ordinary case, or a gateway-managed doctype. It must be a real Frappe document type, because submitting is the moment this becomes a claim on real credit and the document IS the evidence — see _require_evidence_of_payment.

fields.label: Payment Document
fields.description: The document that settled this proposal, in the type named above. The doctype pair is checked for existence at submit, so a settlement cannot claim a payment that is not on the books.

fields.label: Payment Reference
fields.description: What the payment itself is identified by: the bank's transaction reference, the payment gateway's transaction id, or the receipt number issued at the desk. Required for a settlement made by hand, because it is the only trace of money that arrived without a system vouching for it; optional when a gateway transaction already evidences the payment.

fields.label: Expires At
fields.description: When an unpaid proposal stops being claimable. Set by the deployment and stored here, so both sides agree on the deadline.

fields.label: Settled By
fields.description: Who submitted this settlement. On a gateway path this is a script's user rather than a person; either way it is recorded, because 'who made this claimable' must always be answerable.

fields.label: Settlement Note
fields.description: Anything the settler must record: a cash receipt number, a gateway reference, or why an EXPIRED proposal was settled late.

fields.label: Quote Variance (minor)
fields.description: Settled amount minus quoted amount. Non-zero means the money that arrived differs from the quote, which is recorded rather than hidden.

name: Rest Credit Proposal
